title: Hotels Think They Pay 15-25% Commission. They Don't.
hook_line: Independent hotels think they're paying 15 to 25 percent commission to Booking.com and Expedia.
cliffhanger_line: Once you add in the loyalty programs, that number goes somewhere else entirely — and it's not the only cost hiding in there.
pinned_comment: Full commission breakdown (and the cancellation-rate finding nobody talks about) in the full episode — link in bio.
why: Opens with the gap between the commission hotels think they pay and the real rate; withholds the cancellation-rate data and the dollar-loss model that resolve it in long-form.

title: I Ran a Resort With Fifty People. A B&B Owner Has One.
hook_line: At a property I ran, we had fifty people just to keep one booking flow together.
cliffhanger_line: A single owner running a ten-room B&B doesn't have fifty people. So what actually replaces them?
pinned_comment: The answer's in the full episode — what stands in for the headcount a small hotel will never hire.
why: Founder story frames the manpower gap as the real problem; cuts before the video names the agent task force that fills it.

title: Nobody in This Industry Publishes a Price
hook_line: Four of the biggest outsourced revenue-management providers in hospitality. None of them list a price.
cliffhanger_line: Every one quotes privately, deal by deal, after a sales call. So what should this actually cost a hotel?
pinned_comment: We priced it — full breakdown and the number we landed on in the full episode.
why: Surfaces the pricing opacity in the market as the hook; withholds the licensing cost and pricing framework that answer the question.

title: A Booking Engine Was Never the Fix
hook_line: The old fix for hotel commission bleed was a better booking engine. Rate parity, a faster site, catch the guest already looking.
cliffhanger_line: A booking engine doesn't generate demand on its own. Something has to keep pushing traffic toward it — and it's not a marketing hire.
pinned_comment: What actually does that job (it's not one bot answering the phone) — full breakdown in the episode.
why: Reframes the market's assumed fix as wrong; withholds the specific agent roles that answer 'what does the job instead.'
